title: Holcim · Commercial earthworks and logistics yard

turns.speaker: Holcim
turns.text: Jamie explores Knowledge & resources on the Holcim website.
turns.note: Product information helps the customer frame an enquiry before speaking to Sales.
turns.detail: Actual website navigation, followed by the captured enquiry form.
turns.title: Find the right starting point
turns.label: Moment 01

turns.speaker: Holcim
turns.text: Jamie selects Make an enquiry and reaches the contact form.
turns.note: The website gives the customer a direct route to ask for project advice.
turns.title: From browsing to an enquiry
turns.label: Moment 02

turns.speaker: Holcim
turns.text: Jamie Taylor · Riverside Construction · Rugby Logistics Yard · 250 tonnes of MOT Type 1.
turns.note: The customer supplies the information Sales needs to begin a useful callback.
turns.detail: The form-entry section plays at 1.5×. Date, postcode and delivery timing remain blank because they were not supplied.
turns.title: Capture the project and callback details
turns.label: Moment 03

turns.speaker: Holcim
turns.text: Jamie requests a call to discuss supply and pricing for the hardstanding project.
turns.note: The enquiry records a clear next step, alongside permission to contact the customer.
turns.title: Ask Sales to follow up
turns.label: Moment 04

turns.speaker: Holcim
turns.text: Jamie clicks Send enquiry. The website confirms successful submission.
turns.note: The submitted enquiry becomes a contact in the configured Genesys Cloud contact list.
turns.detail: The actual successful submission is retained. It creates a contact; the separate outbound campaign delivers the callback.
turns.title: Send the enquiry into Genesys
turns.label: Moment 05

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: Holcim Servicing Preview is the campaign used for the website follow-up.
turns.note: A preview campaign gives the agent the enquiry context before dialling.
turns.detail: The campaign is shown off in this administration clip. The unrelated training campaign row is hidden only in the edited video.
turns.title: The outbound campaign connects the workflow
turns.label: Moment 06

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: The configuration links the contact list, Holcim queue and outbound follow-up script.
turns.note: These settings determine which enquiry is delivered and which context the agent sees.
turns.detail: Configuration is inspected without changing its stored settings.
turns.title: A campaign configured for Holcim follow-up
turns.label: Moment 07

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: Holcim Servicing Contacts holds the submitted customer record.
turns.note: The contact list is the handoff between website submission and outbound work.
turns.detail: The unrelated training list row is hidden only in this edited video.
turns.title: Find the website enquiry list
turns.label: Moment 08

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: The contact-list configuration leads to Edit Contacts.
turns.note: The agent administrator can inspect the stored enquiry before campaign delivery.
turns.title: Open the contact records
turns.label: Moment 09

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: Jamie Taylor’s record contains the Rugby project, MOT Type 1 and 250 tonnes.
turns.note: The record carries the original website information into the follow-up workflow.
turns.detail: The real captured record is shown; this edit does not change any field values.
turns.title: The submitted details are present
turns.label: Moment 10

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: The contact’s phone column contains +447402159501.
turns.note: The stored callback number completes the route from website enquiry to the customer.
turns.detail: Callable values are stored contact defaults. Their presence alone does not show that a campaign is running.
turns.title: Verify the callback number
turns.label: Moment 11

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: The preview interaction brings Jamie’s stored project and callback details into the agent workspace.
turns.note: The new take begins with campaign delivery and the callback setup. The original website and contact-list sequence is retained above.
turns.title: The website enquiry reaches Sales
turns.label: Moment 12

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: Hi, this is Jamie.
turns.note: Jamie answers the outbound call. The recorded phone follows the same moment as the agent workspace.
turns.title: Jamie answers the callback
turns.label: Moment 13

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: Hi Jamie, this is Emily Carter from the Holcim Sales team, you made an enquiry on our website earlier about a project you're currently working on.
turns.note: Emily connects the conversation to the website enquiry. The recognised brand wording is preserved in the live transcript.
turns.title: Emily follows up the website enquiry
turns.label: Moment 14

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: Hi Emily. Yea, I need 250 tonnes of MOT Type 1 aggregate dropped at a new logistics yard near Rugby. Just need it to prep the hardstanding.
turns.note: Jamie confirms the materials and site. Copilot has already marked one checklist item; the agent still reviews what has actually been confirmed.
turns.title: Confirm the aggregate and destination
turns.label: Moment 15

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: I can get that sorted for you. 250 tonnes to Rugby. While I put that through, are you laying standard asphalt over the top, or have you got specific drainage requirements for this site?
turns.note: Emily repeats 250 tonnes and Rugby, then asks about asphalt and drainage. A recycled-aggregate result is available for inspection.
turns.title: Ask about surfacing and drainage
turns.label: Moment 16

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: The council is breathing down our necks about surface water runoff, to be honest. We need some sort of sustainable drainage for the car park, plus a really heavy-duty slab for the lorry loading bays.
turns.note: The wider drainage and loading-bay needs emerge. Copilot marks 4/4 before the later product explanations; completion marks need agent review.
turns.title: Discover the drainage and loading-bay need
turns.label: Moment 17

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: HC KA 02 appears for the car-park runoff and loading-bay requirements, then the agent opens the article.
turns.note: The opened article explains the wider drainage design and approved slab requirements. Checklist marks remain a review aid.
turns.title: Review the drainage and slab guidance
turns.label: Moment 18

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: Right, for the drainage, you'll want to look at our SuperDrain Asphalt. It's a permeable surface, so the water drains straight through it into the sub-base. It keeps the council happy and saves digging extra drainage channels.
turns.note: The HC KA 02 result brings SuperDrain, drainage design and the related slab opportunity into the same workflow. The recorded product claims remain subject to technical review.
turns.title: Explain the permeable asphalt option
turns.label: Moment 19

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: Never used that before. Does it actually work?
turns.note: The customer asks for reassurance. The live transcript keeps the recognised words and original customer label.
turns.title: The customer asks for reassurance
turns.label: Moment 20

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: It does, it's fully SuDS compliant. And for the lorry bays, we can supply a steel fibre-reinforced concrete. You won't even need to lay steel mesh, which will save your lads a lot of time on site.
turns.note: Emily discusses fibre-reinforced concrete for loading bays. The knowledge guidance calls for an approved design; the recorded dialogue is retained unchanged.
turns.title: Discuss the loading-bay concrete
turns.label: Moment 21

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: Sounds spot on. Get your technical bloke to give me a ring about that slab pour, and send the prices over for the rest.
turns.note: Jamie asks for prices and a technical-team call about the slab. These remain requested next steps.
turns.title: Agree prices and a technical callback
turns.label: Moment 22

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: I'll send the prices over and ask our technical team to give you a ring about the slab. Is there anything else I can help with?
turns.note: Emily confirms the pricing and technical follow-up. Highpave guidance appears alongside the recognised request.
turns.title: Confirm the next step
turns.label: Moment 23

turns.speaker: Jamie · Customer
turns.text: No, that's all, thanks. Have a great day.
turns.note: Jamie confirms there is nothing further and closes the enquiry.
turns.title: Jamie signs off
turns.label: Moment 24

turns.speaker: Emily · Agent
turns.text: You too, Jamie. Bye.
turns.note: Emily closes the call. The next recorded section shows the actual after-call review.
turns.title: Emily closes the conversation
turns.label: Moment 25

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: Genesys generates a draft summary and suggested wrap-up codes while keeping the transcript and checklist available.
turns.note: The actual generation wait is retained. Section outlines follow the new after-call layout.
turns.title: After-call support begins
turns.label: Moment 26

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: The draft captures the Rugby aggregate enquiry, SuperDrain discussion, loading-bay slab and technical follow-up.
turns.note: Generated text is unchanged, including “250 tons” and the recorded product recommendations. The agent reviews the draft before completing wrap-up.
turns.title: Review the generated summary
turns.label: Moment 27

turns.speaker: Genesys
turns.text: Sales - Quote requested is selected. The agent scrolls the summary and submits Done.
turns.note: Technical follow-up and Quote provided are other suggestions. The selected outcome is a quotation request; no completed order is shown.
turns.title: Record the requested quotation
turns.label: Moment 28

Checklist review · 4/4 retained for after-call review

recordingNote: The website enquiry and Genesys campaign/contact-list clips are preserved from the existing Scenario 2, including its approved 1.5× form entry and masks over unrelated training rows. Only the agent experience is replaced, using 22 October take 2: raw agent seconds 33–194 at normal speed, through Done. The full new workspace is preserved; the older wide prefix is proportionally letterboxed. The simultaneous recorded customer phone retains its original bezel, notch, clock and home indicator, and is shown only during the replacement call section. Twelve existing prepared voice clips, pinned before recording, are individually aligned to this take; captured system audio is timing evidence only. No new speech is synthesized. Live transcription, unknown customer labels, early checklist marks and generated summary remain unchanged. The checklist reaches 4/4 before product explanations. Technical product claims in the recorded dialogue and summary require project-specific review. No previous-take after-call content, held frame, recovery footage or reconstructed screen is inserted.
